text:
hana: Quick kickoff  I'm drafting a single "Scale Policy Index" page that links out to provisioning, reserved pools, and the autoscale examples we scatter around. Goal: reduce duplicated snippets and make a single source-of-truth for policy YAML, TF mapping, SDK calls, and eviction rules. Tagging @kevin @mona for review.

kevin: Love the idea. Can we add a tiny decision table telling teams when to pick steady vs reactive vs reserved-pool? That reduces product questions.

mona: Yes. Also request: show a short example of label precedence so teams understand eviction outcomes when multiple labels exist. That is the #1 confusing bit in support tickets.

hana: Plan: sections -> overview, decision table, canonical YAML examples (steady/burst/reserved), TF + Go + Python snippets, eviction precedence algorithm, short FAQ, and a one-line SLA blurb to reuse across pages. I'll open a PR shortly.

kevin: For the eviction algorithm, please include both pseudocode and a tiny real example. Something like: final_score = min(isolation_base, tenant_override) and a worked example.

mona: I'll paste a minimal burst YAML and a Go snippet we can include. Also recommend the TF example use jsonencode(policy) so readers don't get tripped by HCL mapping.

```yaml
# burst example
scalePolicy:
  name: burst-payments
  type: reactive
  targets:
    cpu_utilization: 0.8
  burst:
    max_instances: 6
    cooldown: 45s
  labels:
    tenant: "payments"
    isolation: "shared"
```

```go
// Go SDK snippet (minimal)
client := redwood.NewClient(os.Getenv("RW_KEY"))
_, err := client.Dedicated.CreateScalePolicy(ctx, redwood.CreateScalePolicyParams{
  PoolID: "pool-42",
  Name:  "burst-payments",
  Policy: redwood.Policy{Type: "reactive", Targets: map[string]float64{"cpu":0.8}},
})
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
```

kevin: Nice. For Python, keep it short and show labels argument. I can paste one if useful. Also add a note about cooldown formatting: prefer strings like "45s" in examples.

mona: Small eviction precedence example I'll add to the page:

- isolation_base: dedicated=10, shared=80
- tenant_reserved_override: payments=5 if assigned to reserved-pool
- effective = min(isolation_base, tenant_reserved_override)

Worked example: isolation=shared (80) + tenant_reserved_override=5 => effective=5 (tenant reservation wins).

kevin: Good. Docs-bot: please run linkcheck on any anchors you add; our TF anchors keep drifting.

docs-bot: Draft PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/4999 - scale-policy-index. CI: docs-lint passing, linkcheck: 1 broken anchor detected -> /docs/dedicated/faq#eviction-rules (anchor missing).

hana: I'll update the target page or adjust the anchor in the PR. Will hold merge until linkcheck is green.

legal-bot: Canonical SLA wording (approved): "Reserved pools are SLA-backed for availability and latency targets. Reactive autoscale policies are best-effort and are not covered by reserved-pool SLAs." Use this sentence verbatim in dedicated pages.

ops-bot: Ops note: include a troubleshooting checklist under the big example: 1) label mismatch, 2) pool quota, 3) warmup window, 4) KV/prefix caching reducing CPU and delaying reactive triggers. That list maps to the majority of evictions tickets.

kevin: Suggest UI cross-link: add a small badge on the provisioning page that points to the Scale Policy Index so readers jump straight to examples.

hana: Agree. I'll add a tiny badge + a short changelog at the bottom listing removed/relocated snippets to help discoverability. Plan to merge after anchor fix and a quick pass from @mona on formatting. ETA EOD.

mona: Happy to review formatting and TF jsonencode guidance. Will check in ~30m.

hana: Thanks all. Tagging reviewers: @kevin @mona. Will post PR link here when pushed. :rocket:
